page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is an x86_64 Cloud Compute server featuring 4 shared Intel Xeon vCPUs, mapped from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tiers of compute capability. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the server in the bottom 25% or bottom 10% of tested hardware. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is average at 367.64 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET performance are weak to poor, with Redis achieving 2.63 million operations per second.

Given the shared CPU allocation and modest performance metrics, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated hardware threads. It is suitable for lightweight tasks such as static web serving, basic development environments, and simple background processing. It is not recommended for high-throughput databases, intensive data processing, or large language model inference due to its constrained memory bandwidth and lower CPU execution speeds.
